A.depoimento: I am splitting my forces to assault both Santarem and Evora simultaneously, aiming to secure two neutral villages in a single turn and gain a strong economic foothold. I also build an archer at Lisboa to prepare for the next wave of expansion once the attacks succeed.
A.plano: Expand rapidly to the neighboring neutral villages of Santarem and Evora to secure resources and a multi-front foothold. I am splitting my current forces to assault both villages simultaneously, leaving Lisboa temporarily empty but building an archer to reinforce next turn. Once Santarem and Evora fall, I will push towards Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro to build a strong economic and military base to eventually dominate the 24-village map.

A.depoimento: Orders given: Santarem splits to take Coimbra and Badajoz; Evora sends a strong force to Faro. Lisboa builds a knight and sends its archer to Santarem. The traps are set; by dawn, the neutral southern and central villages will be ours, and our borders will stretch deep into the peninsula!
A.plano: Conquer Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro this turn to secure a strong foothold and open up the central and southern routes. Split Santarem's forces to take Coimbra and Badajoz, and Evora's forces to take Faro. Build a knight in Lisboa to reinforce the capital and prepare for the next wave of expansion towards Porto, Salamanca, and Sevilha.

B.depoimento: I am launching a double attack on the neutral villages of Tarragona and Girona to secure my borders and increase my resource production. I have carefully allocated my troops to minimize losses, sending a spearman-heavy force to Tarragona and an archer-heavy force to Girona. I am also building 4 more spearmen in Barcelona to reinforce my capital.
B.plano: Capture Tarragona and Girona this turn to expand my territory and boost my economy. Build 4 spearmen in Barcelona for next turn's defense and expansion. Explore the road network next turn to locate the enemy.

A.depoimento: We launched a decisive strike on Sevilha, hoping to break the southern neutral line. Our forces in Faro left a knight behind and charged with spearmen and archers. We reinforced Coimbra and Faro, and started building up our army in the capital and other villages for the next push.
A.plano: This turn we attack Sevilha with the southern army to break the southern neutral line. We send 1 spear, 2 archers, 1 knight from Faro, keeping 1 knight in Faro. We reinforce Coimbra with an archer from Santarem to prepare for an attack on Porto. We send Evora's spearman to Faro to reinforce after the attack. We send Lisboa's knight to Santarem as a staging point. We build 1 archer and 1 spearman in Lisboa, 2 spearmen in Santarem, and 1 archer in Evora to grow our army. Next turns we will consolidate Sevilha, build there, and push towards Cordoba or Porto depending on enemy movements.

B.depoimento: I have ordered my armies in Tarragona and Girona to strike at the neutral villages of Castellon and Huesca respectively, while Barcelona begins training a knight to bolster our forces.
B.plano: Capture Castellon and Huesca to expand my territory and boost my economy. Build a knight in Barcelona for future offensive power. Next turn, explore further south towards Zaragoza and the enemy capital.

A.depoimento: This turn we ordered a coordinated strike: Coimbra's forces attack Porto while the southern army assaults Sevilha. Reinforcements from Lisboa, Santarem, Badajoz, and Faro rush to support the attack. Our forges produce new archers, spearmen, and knights to feed the war machine.
A.plano: We are launching a two-front assault. The southern army from Faro, reinforced by Badajoz, will take Sevilha and then push towards Cordoba and the southern plains. The northern army from Coimbra, reinforced by Santarem and Lisboa, will capture Porto and advance to Vigo and Salamanca. We are building troops in all villages to sustain the offensive. Our goal is to capture 18 villages quickly, focusing on the weak neutral clusters and avoiding the enemy capital for now.

B.depoimento: Orders given: marched on Zaragoza and Valencia with full force. Both neutral villages fell easily. Built new spearman in our northern and eastern villages to secure the borders and prepare for further expansion into the unexplored south.
B.plano: Conquer Zaragoza and Valencia this turn to expand territory and boost economy. Send all troops from Huesca to Zaragoza and from Castellon to Valencia. Build spearman in Barcelona, Tarragona, and Girona to reinforce the newly conquered and existing villages for next turn.

A.depoimento: Our southern army from Sevilha assaults Cordoba. Reinforcements from Santarem, Badajoz, Faro, and Evora move to strengthen our fronts. We build troops in our villages to fuel the expansion.
A.plano: We are launching a two-front assault. The southern army from Sevilha takes Cordoba this turn. We reinforce Coimbra and Porto to prepare for attacks on Salamanca and Vigo next turn. We also reinforce Sevilha and Badajoz to hold new territories. Build troops in all villages. Next turn, attack Salamanca from Coimbra and Vigo from Porto, then push into the unexplored areas.

B.depoimento: We attack Teruel and Madrid to expand our kingdom. Our armies march to conquer, and we build more troops for the next battles.
B.plano: Attack Teruel from Valencia and Madrid from Zaragoza with all available troops. Build a mix of spearman, archers, and knights to reinforce next turn. After capturing, send reinforcements to hold the new villages and continue expanding.

A.depoimento: This turn, we attacked on three fronts, taking Salamanca, Toledo, and Vigo from the neutrals. We sent reinforcements from our rear villages to the front and built new troops to replace losses and prepare for the next push.
A.plano: Over the next turns, we will consolidate our gains by reinforcing the newly captured villages. We will then push east from Salamanca towards Madrid, from Toledo towards Teruel, and from Vigo towards Burgos. We will build up our army in the rear and use our knights for rapid strikes. Our goal is to capture 18 villages to secure victory.

B.depoimento: Our armies captured Salamanca and Toledo, expanding our realm to 11 villages. We built archers and a knight across the land, preparing for the next pushes.
B.plano: Attack Salamanca from Madrid and Toledo from Teruel with all available troops. Build archers in every village with iron to counter spearman villages; build a knight at Zaragoza for the next attack on Pamplona. Next turn, reinforce the new captures and prepare to attack Pamplona and Burgos.

A.depoimento: This turn, we coordinated a multi-pronged attack. A strong force from Coimbra follows up the assault on Salamanca, while Badajoz and Cordoba launch a counter-offensive to retake Toledo. Reinforcements from our interior villages stream to the border, ensuring our armies are ready for the next push. Our builders work overtime, producing knights and archers to sustain the campaign.
A.plano: This turn we focus on taking Salamanca and retaking Toledo. We send a second wave from Coimbra to Salamanca and attack Toledo from Badajoz and Cordoba. Reinforcements flow from the interior to the front lines: Santarem and Lisboa reinforce Coimbra; Faro, Sevilha, and Vigo reinforce Porto and Badajoz. Our builds prioritize knights and archers to maintain a balanced army. After securing these villages, we will turn to the neutral villages of Burgos and Murcia, then push east towards Madrid and the enemy capital. We must keep building troops and moving them to the front to maintain momentum.

B.depoimento: The enemy is attacking Salamanca. We are building archers to counter their spearmen and moving troops to reinforce our borders and prepare for counter-attacks on Murcia, Burgos, and Cordoba.
B.plano: We are building archers in all villages with iron to counter enemy spearmen. We are sending Toledo's troops to Salamanca to reinforce/retake, Zaragoza's troops to Madrid to project power, and Castellon's troops to Valencia to gather forces for attacking Murcia. We must hold our borders and prepare to attack Burgos and Cordoba next.

A.depoimento: Our knights capture Teruel, securing an eastern foothold. We march a strong force from Porto to Burgos to claim the neutral village. We flood Salamanca with reinforcements from Badajoz, Coimbra, and Porto, building a massive army for Madrid. We reinforce Cordoba and reshape its garrison for Murcia. We build knights and archers across our realm to grow our strength.
A.plano: Plan: We take Teruel with knights from Toledo. We send a strong force from Porto to Burgos to capture it. We heavily reinforce Salamanca for the upcoming Madrid attack. We reinforce Cordoba and reshape its garrison for Murcia. We build knights and archers everywhere. Next turn we attack Madrid and Murcia, while Burgos falls. Then we push east to reach 18 villages.

B.depoimento: Turn 9: Our armies are on the move to capture the neutral villages of Murcia, Pamplona, and Burgos. Valencia's forces march on Murcia, while Huesca's archers and knights head to Pamplona. In the north, Zaragoza's knights ride to Madrid to reinforce our forces for the assault on Burgos. We are building knights in our capitals and archers along the borders to strengthen our economy and military. The enemy is distracted on the western front, and we will exploit this to expand our territory.
B.plano: We are focusing on capturing the three neutral villages: Murcia, Pamplona, and Burgos, to increase our village count to 12. We are sending Valencia's troops to Murcia, Huesca's archers and knight to Pamplona, and reinforcing Madrid with Zaragoza's knights to prepare for the attack on Burgos. We are building knights in our capital and major cities, and archers/spearmen in our border villages to defend and project power. Next turn, we will attack Murcia and Burgos, and continue marching to Pamplona.

B.depoimento: We struck at Burgos with a knight-archer force from Madrid to claim the last neutral village. We rushed reinforcements to Castellon, Zaragoza, and Valencia to shore up our defenses against the enemy's newly conquered Teruel. Across the realm, our villages worked to produce a new generation of knights for the campaign ahead.
B.plano: We are attacking Burgos with knights and archers from Madrid to secure the neutral village before the enemy can take it. We are reinforcing our border villages of Castellon, Zaragoza, and Valencia with troops from Tarragona, Huesca, and Murcia to defend against enemy counter-attacks from Teruel. We are building knights in all our major villages to replenish our forces.

A.depoimento: King A orders the assault on Madrid! The army of Salamanca marches to crush the enemy neighbor, while reinforcements rush to Cordoba, Teruel, and Vigo to secure our borders and set the stage for total victory.
A.plano: Focus on the central front. This turn, launch a major assault on Madrid from Salamanca, leaving a solid garrison of 9 troops to defend it. Simultaneously, reinforce all other border villages (Cordoba, Teruel, Vigo) from their interior allies to prepare for next turn's offensives on Murcia, Valencia, and Burgos. Build troops in all villages to maintain momentum and replace losses.

B.depoimento: Turn 11: Our armies are on the move! We march on Vigo to claim it, while wisely reinforcing our borders at Madrid and Murcia. The interior villages send their finest troops to the front lines, and our forges burn day and night crafting knights and archers. We grow stronger, ready to strike when the time is right.
B.plano: We are attacking Vigo from Burgos to expand our territory. We are reinforcing Murcia from Valencia and Madrid from Zaragoza to strengthen our borders. We are sending reinforcements to Castellon and Zaragoza to prepare for a major offensive next turn. We are building knights and archers in all our villages to grow our army. We are not attacking Teruel this turn to avoid heavy losses from Toledo reinforcement.

A.depoimento: Taking Burgos with a double thrust from Madrid and Vigo while reinforcing Madrid from Salamanca and Teruel from Toledo. Building troops across all villages to grow my army for the next offensives on Valencia and Murcia.
A.plano: Take Burgos this turn with a double thrust: knight from Madrid and knight from Vigo. Reinforce Madrid with 2 knights from Salamanca and Teruel with 2 knights + 3 archers from Toledo. Build troops in all 14 villages (4 knights, 18 archers) to grow the army. Next turn, attack Valencia from Teruel using spearmen for the counter bonus against their knights, and Murcia from Cordoba using knights for the counter bonus against their archers. Continue building and pushing east to reach 18 villages.

B.depoimento: King B's armies attack Vigo, Teruel, and Madrid simultaneously. Reinforcements rush to bolster our weakest defenses. Our builders work overtime, forging a new generation of spearman and knight. The fate of the realm hangs in the balance.
B.plano: We are attacking Vigo, Teruel, and Madrid to expand our territory. We are reinforcing our weak border villages to improve our defenses. We are building mostly spearmen and some knights to grow our army. We hope to conquer three villages this turn.

B.depoimento: This turn, I am focusing my strikes on the weakly defended Burgos and the heavily guarded Teruel. I am sending my Pamplona spearmen to conquer Burgos, while reinforcing them from Zaragoza. Simultaneously, I am launching a dual-wave assault on Teruel to chip away at their knights and archers. At home, I am converting my resources into a massive wave of knights to ensure we have the speed and firepower to dominate the battlefield next turn.
B.plano: Focus on conquering the weak enemy village [14] Burgos using the spearmen from [19] Pamplona. Reinforce [19] with spearmen from [17] Zaragoza to prepare for further advances westward. Launch a double-pronged attack on [13] Teruel from [18] Castellon and [16] Valencia to wear down its heavy garrison. Build knights in all major villages to build up a fast-moving strike force for next turn.

B.depoimento: We have successfully conquered Burgos, securing a vital foothold in the north. Recognizing the heavy losses from our recent assaults on Teruel and Cordoba, I am shifting our strategy. We will focus on the weakly defended Vigo, reinforcing Burgos with troops from Pamplona. By building knights across our empire, we prepare a swift and overwhelming strike force to break the enemy's western flank.
B.plano: Focus on conquering the weak enemy village [10] Vigo. Send all available troops from Pamplona [19] to Burgos [14] to reinforce it. Build knights in all major villages, especially Burgos and Pamplona, to build up a fast-moving strike force. Next turn, launch a combined attack on Vigo from Burgos. Do not attack Teruel or Cordoba until we have a larger army.

B.depoimento: This turn, I ordered a double-pronged attack to expand our territory. From Burgos, our spearman and knight march to conquer the weak enemy village of Vigo. From Castellon, our archers and knights march to assault Teruel, aiming to break the enemy's eastern border. Simultaneously, I have ordered the construction of knights across our interior villages—Pamplona, Tarragona, Girona, Huesca, and Murcia—along with Castellon, to build a highly mobile strike force. We also build archers in Zaragoza and Barcelona, and spearmen in Burgos and Valencia, to maintain a balanced army. We must keep pushing to
B.plano: Conquer Vigo [10] from Burgos [14] and Teruel [13] from Castellon [18] this turn to expand our territory and weaken King A. Build knights in all interior villages (Pamplona, Tarragona, Girona, Huesca, Murcia) and Castellon to build up a fast-moving strike force. Build archers in Zaragoza and Barcelona, and spearmen in Burgos and Valencia to round out our infantry. Next turn, reinforce Madrid [12] or Cordoba [11] for further attacks. Do not leave border villages undefended.

A.depoimento: We are strengthening our defenses along the border while launching an assault on Murcia. Our armies are marching to reinforce our allies, and our builders are working hard to produce more troops. We will continue to press the advantage and expand our territory.
A.plano: This turn we reinforce our border villages: Salamanca to Madrid, Coimbra to Porto, Badajoz to Toledo, Sevilha to Cordoba. We launch an attack on Murcia from Cordoba with all available troops. We build archers at Madrid, Toledo, Porto, Cordoba, and other villages to increase our strength. Next turn, we will have a strong garrison at Cordoba and can attack Valencia from Murcia. We will also consider attacking Burgos from Madrid once we have enough troops. Our goal is to capture 18 villages and hold them for two turns.

A.depoimento: This turn we launch a three-pronged attack on Burgos, Valencia, and Vigo. We reinforce our border villages from our interior lands and build up our armies. We are expanding our territory towards victory.
A.plano: We attack Burgos, Valencia, and Vigo this turn. We send reinforcements from interior villages to our border: Salamanca to Madrid, Coimbra to Porto, Badajoz to Toledo, Sevilha to Cordoba, Cordoba to Murcia, Faro to Sevilha. We build troops at all villages. After these attacks, we will have 16 villages and will prepare to attack Teruel and Zaragoza to reach 18, then hold for two turns.

B.depoimento: This turn, we mobilized our forces to strike at the enemy's weakest points. We sent armies from Valencia, Vigo, and Teruel to conquer Murcia, Porto, and Toledo respectively. Simultaneously, we reinforced our border villages of Zaragoza and Burgos to prepare for the next phase of our campaign against Madrid.
B.plano: We are launching a three-pronged attack on Murcia, Porto, and Toledo to secure our borders and expand our territory. We have sent reinforcements to Zaragoza and Burgos to prepare for the assault on Madrid next turn. We must ensure our newly conquered villages are fortified quickly to prevent enemy counter-attacks.

A.depoimento: We launched a three-front offensive this turn, sending our best troops to take Vigo, Burgos, and Valencia. Reinforcements from interior villages rushed to the front lines to support the assault and hold the gains. Our armies march to conquer three enemy villages and bring us closer to victory.
A.plano: This turn: attack Vigo (from Porto), Burgos (from Madrid), Valencia (from Murcia). Send reinforcements from interior villages to all front lines. Expect to reach 16 villages. Next turn: attack Teruel from Toledo and Pamplona from Burgos to reach 18, then hold for two turns to win. Build troops at every village.

A.depoimento: I launched a successful double attack, taking Teruel and Valencia. I have ordered all rear villages to march to the front, concentrating our forces for the decisive assault on Pamplona next turn. With these moves, we will reach the 18-village threshold and secure the crown.
A.plano: Attack Teruel from Toledo and Valencia from Murcia this turn to reach 17 villages. Send all interior troops to the front lines (Toledo, Madrid, Burgos, Murcia) to prepare for the final push on Pamplona next turn, which will bring us to 18 villages. Then hold the line for two turns to secure victory. Build troops everywhere to replenish losses.

B.depoimento: King B's forces struck at Madrid today, sending a dozen knights to conquer the enemy city. Meanwhile, our borders are being reinforced as we send troops to Pamplona, Teruel, and Valencia, setting the stage for a triple assault on Burgos, Toledo, and Murcia next turn. The enemy will not know what hit them!
B.plano: We launched a strong attack on Madrid with 12 knights, expecting to conquer it this turn. Simultaneously, we sent reinforcements from Zaragoza, Huesca, Castellon, and Teruel to Pamplona, Valencia, and Teruel to set up decisive attacks on Burgos, Murcia, and Toledo next turn. We must check if Madrid fell and then coordinate the triple assault. Continue building troops in all villages to sustain the momentum.

A.depoimento: We stood fast at Teruel against the enemy's assault, sending reinforcements from the interior to the front. Our armies are marching on Madrid and will take it next turn. We're building our forces for the final push to 18 villages.
A.plano: This turn, we defend Teruel against the enemy attack and reinforce our border villages with interior troops. Next turn, our armies take Madrid (16 villages). Then we attack Castellon from Teruel (17) and Valencia from Murcia (18). We hold for two turns to win. Build troops everywhere to replenish losses.

B.depoimento: We reinforced Madrid from Zaragoza to prepare for the two incoming enemy armies. We launched an assault on Murcia from Valencia to conquer our 10th village. We sent reinforcements to Valencia and Zaragoza to secure our borders. We are building troops across all villages to maintain our military momentum.
B.plano: Defend Madrid by sending all available troops from Zaragoza. Attack Murcia from Valencia to expand our territory. Reinforce Valencia from Castellon, and Zaragoza from Pamplona and Huesca. Build troops in all villages to sustain the army. Do not move troops from Madrid until the enemy armies are repelled. Check the outcome of the Teruel march.

A.depoimento: This turn we launch a strike on Castellon from Teruel, sending a fast force of knights and archers to take the weakly defended enemy village. Simultaneously, we march reinforcements from Toledo and other interior villages to our border towns of Cordoba, Teruel, and Madrid, strengthening our defenses and preparing for the next pushes into Murcia and Valencia. Our troops build across the empire as we move to capture three more villages and win the war.
A.plano: We attack Castellon from Teruel this turn with 4 knights and 2 archers to capture our 16th village. We send reinforcements from Toledo to Cordoba, Teruel, and Madrid to secure borders and prepare for attacks on Murcia and Valencia. We build troops everywhere to replenish forces. Next turn we take Valencia and Murcia to reach 18 villages and win.

B.depoimento: We are launching a decisive double-pronged assault on the lightly defended Cordoba to secure our southern expansion route. At the same time, we are consolidating our northern forces into Zaragoza to fortify our central borders and prepare for the inevitable clash with Madrid.
B.plano: Focus on conquering Cordoba [11] using the troops from Murcia and Valencia to open the path to the south. Simultaneously, mass all available troops from Pamplona, Huesca, and Tarragona into Zaragoza [17] to create an unbreakable defensive line and prepare for the next offensive push. Build troops across all villages to sustain our war machine.

B.depoimento: This turn, we mobilized our forces to prepare for a decisive strike against Castellon. We marched spearman from Zaragoza and archers from Barcelona to Tarragona, forming a spearhead to counter the enemy's knights and break through their southern border. At the same time, we consolidated our troops from Pamplona, Huesca, and Girona into Zaragoza, fortifying our capital as the springboard for the next phase of our campaign. Our war machine continues to build across all villages, ready to strike again soon.
B.plano: Focus on conquering Castellon [18] first as it is the weakest enemy border village (defense 13). We are massing a spearman-heavy army at Tarragona [21] by sending 10 spearmen and 2 archers from Zaragoza [17], and all available troops (5 archers, 1 knight) from Barcelona [22]. This spearman army will counter Castellon's knights and easily conquer it on Turn 24. Simultaneously, we are sending all available troops from Pamplona [19], Huesca [20], and Girona [23] to Zaragoza [17] to create an unbreakable defensive line and prepare the next offensive push. Build troops across all villages to sustai

A.depoimento: My armies strike on three fronts simultaneously, targeting the weakly defended enemy villages of Murcia, Valencia, and Pamplona. With overwhelming force and the archer counter bonus against Pamplona's spearmen, I expect decisive victories. This will bring my total to 18 villages, putting me on the path to victory.
A.plano: Capture Murcia, Valencia, and Pamplona this turn to reach 18 villages. Garrison the new territories with the surviving attackers. Replenish the border villages (Cordoba, Teruel, Burgos) by building archers locally and sending reinforcements from Toledo and Salamanca next turn. Prepare to assault the enemy stronghold Zaragoza from Madrid, Teruel, and Pamplona in the following turns.

B.depoimento: We launch a decisive strike on Castellon with our full force from Tarragona, aiming to break the enemy's eastern border. Reinforcements are rushed to Zaragoza to guard against counter-attacks from Madrid, while our villages work tirelessly to replenish our ranks.
B.plano: Focus on conquering Castellon [18] with the full force of Tarragona [21]. Send all available troops from Pamplona [19] and Huesca [20] to Zaragoza [17] to reinforce the central front. Rebuild troops across all villages to maintain our offensive capability.

A.depoimento: We are reinforcing Madrid to the teeth, sending every available man from Toledo and Salamanca to make it an unassailable fortress. Meanwhile, we are pushing into Huesca from Pamplona to secure a 19th village, protecting our 75% threshold even if a border village falls. The enemy is being contained on all fronts.
A.plano: Reinforce Madrid with all troops from Toledo and Salamanca to create an unassailable fortress capable of holding against Zaragoza. Send troops from Murcia to Valencia and Burgos to Pamplona to secure the other fronts. Attack Huesca from Pamplona to increase village count to 19, ensuring that even if Pamplona falls, we still hold 18 villages and secure the win condition. Build troops across all villages to rebuild the army for the next phase.

B.depoimento: This turn, I reinforced my borders by sending troops to Huesca and Castellon, and launched an attack on Teruel from Zaragoza. I also built knights in all my villages to strengthen my army. I am focused on securing my eastern flank and expanding into enemy territory.
B.plano: Focus on securing the east by reinforcing Castellon and Huesca. Attacked Teruel from Zaragoza to expand. Built knights across all villages. Next turn: assess Huesca battle, push on Valencia from Castellon, consider attack on Madrid from Zaragoza if it is safe.

A.depoimento: We have launched the decisive attack on Huesca to reclaim our 18th village and secure the 75% victory threshold. While the main army marches to Madrid, we are reinforcing our vulnerable border towns of Toledo and Pamplona to prevent any enemy breakthroughs. Across the realm, our villages are working overtime, forging a fresh legion of knights and archers to swell our ranks once more.
A.plano: The march to Huesca is already underway and will succeed, giving us the 18th village. We must defend Toledo and Pamplona, which are vulnerable after sending out troops. We will reinforce Toledo from Cordoba and Badajoz, and Pamplona from Burgos. We will build knights and archers across all villages to rebuild our army for the next phase of expansion or defense. Once we hold 18 villages for one turn, we must ensure we hold them for the second turn to win.

B.depoimento: I am launching a decisive attack on the weakly defended enemy village of Toledo using my forces from Teruel. I am also reinforcing my northern border by sending a knight from Barcelona to Girona, and bolstering Teruel's garrison with troops from Zaragoza and Castellon. My army is growing, and I am determined to expand my kingdom.
B.plano: Attack Toledo [8] from Teruel [13] with 5 archers and 3 knights to conquer it. Reinforce Girona [23] with Barcelona's [22] knight to prepare for Huesca [20] next turn. Reinforce Teruel [13] with troops from Zaragoza [17] and Castellon [18] for defense. Build troops in all villages to grow the army. Next turn, assess the situation after taking Toledo and plan the next attack (Huesca or Valencia).

B.depoimento: King B's forces have successfully conquered Toledo [8] and now look to expand south. We launch an attack on Cordoba [11] with our elite knights and archers, while reinforcing our borders and building troops across all our villages to prepare for the next push into enemy territory.
B.plano: Attack Cordoba [11] from Toledo [8] with 2 knights and 1 archer to conquer it and expand south. Reinforce Toledo [8] from Teruel [13] with 3 archers and 1 knight, and reinforce Teruel from Zaragoza [17] and Castellon [18] to prepare for the next attack on Badajoz [4] next turn. Build troops in all villages to grow our army.

B.depoimento: King B orders a multi-pronged offensive to conquer Badajoz, Murcia, and Huesca, expanding our territory and weakening King A's hold on the peninsula. Reinforcements are sent to Castellon to secure the border, while all villages work to build up their garrisons for the next phase of the campaign.
B.plano: Attack Badajoz [4] from Toledo [8], Murcia [15] from Cordoba [11], and Huesca [20] from Zaragoza [17] to expand our territory. Reinforce Castellon [18] from Tarragona [21]. Build troops in all villages to grow the army. Next turn, consolidate gains and prepare for the push south towards Sevilha [9] and the enemy capital.

A.depoimento: I launched a double strike on the enemy's weakest positions: Madrid's archers overwhelmed Toledo, while Valencia's forces captured Murcia. I also rushed reinforcements to Salamanca to seal the hole in my western border after last turn's painful losses. The enemy is reeling, and my army is poised to expand further.
A.plano: This turn I strike the enemy's weak points: Madrid's 50-man archer force takes Toledo, while Valencia's troops capture Murcia. I also rush reinforcements from Porto and Coimbra to Salamanca to plug the border hole after last turn's losses. Next turn I will use these new footholds to attack Cordoba and Badajoz, aiming to reach 18 villages. I am building archers and knights across all villages to sustain the army for the next pushes.

B.depoimento: Our forces converge on Salamanca, overwhelming its small garrison. Reinforcements stream to our vulnerable border towns. We build knights across the realm, preparing for the next push south.
B.plano: Attack Salamanca from Badajoz with archers and knight to capture a weak village. Reinforce Huesca from Girona, Zaragoza from Tarragona and Barcelona, and Murcia from Cordoba. Build knights in all villages to grow the army. Next turn, push towards Sevilha and Faro, and consolidate gains.

B.depoimento: I ordered a full assault on Valencia, the weakest enemy village on my eastern border, sending the bulk of Castellon's army to secure it. I rushed reinforcements to Toledo to bolster its defenses against the enemy army marching there. I also reinforced Castellon and Huesca to prepare for further expansion. My villages are building knights to increase my military strength.
B.plano: Attack Valencia from Castellon with most troops to capture a border village and expand my territory. Reinforce Toledo from Teruel and Badajoz to hold against the incoming enemy army. Reinforce Castellon from Tarragona, and Huesca from Girona and Zaragoza to prepare for further pushes. Build knights in all viable villages to grow the army. Next turn, consolidate Valencia and prepare to attack Murcia.
